Subject: Inquiry — Optimize toolkit (batching/kv-cache/quantization) pricing

Hi Neha,

Quick intro — I'm Liam, Head of ML at Citrine Labs. We're evaluating Redwood's Optimize toolkit to reduce inference spend for our recommendation models. Two quick asks we need pricing/packaging for so we can brief procurement: 1) a conservative estimate for monthly unit economics at ~1M generated tokens/month with typical 512-token responses (low-latency target ~150ms p50), and 2) what discounts or packaging options exist if we commit to a 12-month plan and apply Optimize to two clusters (us-east-1 + us-west-2).

Specifically, we care about: batching and KV-prefetch impacts on cost, the recommended quantization profile for bfloat16->int8 tradeoffs, and whether Redwood will provide a migration credit or up-front pilot allowance for the first 3 months.

Can you send a succinct price/packaging sketch (numbers + assumptions) and a short tech appendix we can share with our infra team? We need something by end of week to keep procurement moving.

Thanks —
Liam O'Connor
Head of ML, Citrine Labs
liam@citrine.ai

Hi Liam — great to meet you over email. Thanks for the clear asks.

TL;DR — we can provide:
- Two packaging options: (A) Optimize Add-on (usage-based, no commit) and (B) Annual Optimize Commitment (12-month, discounted bundle with pilot credits).
- Ballpark numbers (assumptions listed below) and a 30-minute call to align on latency and hit-rate expectations.

Ballpark pricing for your stated profile (~1M tokens/month, avg response 512 tokens):
- Optimize Add-on (no commit): $0.015 per optimized token (includes batching & KV caching recommendations); estimated monthly cost: $15k.
- Annual Optimize Commitment (12-month): base unit price $0.010/optimized token; with a 20% volume discount at $0.008/opt-token for a 12-month minimum commit + $50k annual minimum. Estimated monthly spend: $8k–$10k depending on hit rate.

Assumptions (please review):
- KV-cache: we assumed a 40% effective KV hit rate across your requests (higher hit rate reduces cost linearly).
- Batching: average request batching improves throughput; estimates assume steady-state concurrent request profile with p50 latency target 150ms.
- Quantization: recommended path is mixed-int8 (per-layer FP16 fallback) for this model class — typically reduces GPU memory and token cost 1.6x with small accuracy delta.

We can put together a short tech appendix (attachment) with: hit-rate sensitivity table, quantization tradeoffs, and an ops checklist for rollout. I'm attaching a concise pricing summary and copying Dylan (solutions) to add the technical appendix.

Next steps: would you be available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT? If procurement needs a tighter discount to sign, let us know the target range and we can escalate.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Liam / Neha — adding the technical context Dylan here. (short version: numbers above look good with the hit-rate caveat; details below)

Technical appendix (high level):
- KV cache hit-rate: 40% is conservative if you have stable prompts/templates. If you can template >70% of tokens, expect 2–3x cost improvement vs no-cache. We include prefix caching and per-route cache policies in Optimize.
- Batching effects: at p50 150ms we can do small micro-batches (4–8) without increasing p50. If your workload is spiky, effective batch depth will vary — our cost model assumes average batching depth 3.
- Quantization: we recommend an int8 path with per-layer calibration and fallback to fp16 for unstable layers. Expect ~10–15% end-task delta on worst-case generative outputs; most classification/regression tasks see <3% delta.
- Rollout notes: start with Canary on a fraction of traffic (5–10%), measure quality via your eval set (we can run a benchmark), then escalate to full traffic.

I attached a short technical appendix with the calibration steps, test harness snippet (how to measure quality/regression), and a hit-rate sensitivity matrix. Two operational asks for accurate pricing:
1) Provide an estimate of your live prompt variability (how often prompts change per session), and
2) Confirm whether you can accept an int8 quant path for 25% of the model (some customers keep a fp16 replica for edge cases).

Happy to jump on the call Neha proposed.

—Dylan Brooks
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

- Procurement asks whether we can secure a deeper discount for a 12-month commit. Their target is ~40% off the annual list for the first year if we commit to a $100k ARR level.
- From infra: our prompt templates are fairly stable for the recommendation flows (estimated KV hit ~60% after small cleanup). We can accept int8 with fp16 fallback for 30% of traffic initially.
- Timeline: procurement needs final commercial terms and a draft SOW by next Tuesday to make the quarter close.

If Redwood can bridge to ~35–40% first-year discount + a migration credit (we were hoping for $30k), procurement will fast-track. Can you respond with a counter-offer and confirm you can deliver an SOW by next Tue?

Thanks —
Liam
